conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I’ll be taking care of you during your stay. Can you tell me what’s been going on?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Hi, thanks. I’ve had bad stomach cramps and diarrhea for about a month now. It started after I saw some sick kids and then got my IVIG infusion.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. And how frequent are the stools? Any blood or fever?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: A few times a day, liquid at first, but they’re starting to firm up. I had red stools once after red jello, but no more since. No fevers.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that helps. Given your history of lymphoma and immune deficiency, we want to be careful. We’ll run some tests.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve also been feeling dizzy when I stand up. Started a few days ago.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your blood pressure was low in clinic—94 over 55. That could explain the dizziness. We’ll monitor that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my left shoulder’s been hurting for about a week. Was I supposed to get an X-ray before coming in?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, but it wasn’t done. We’ll order that tomorrow so we can check it out.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, thanks. I’m just worried it’s something serious with my lymphoma coming back.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I understand. But your symptoms are more likely due to an infection, especially since others around you were sick.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That makes sense. I’ve been trying to eat more carbs to firm up my stools, but it’s just made my blood sugar worse.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we saw your HbA1c is 7%, so diabetes is under reasonable control. We’ll hold your metformin for now and use insulin as needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Alright. What about my IVIG? I’m due for it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll give it during your stay. It’s important for your immune deficiency. We’ll also start antibiotics just in case.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m allergic to penicillin and sulfa drugs. Just so you know.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Noted. You already got cefepime and flagyl in clinic, which are safe for you. We’ll continue that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your CT scan from yesterday didn’t show any new masses or bowel issues. Lymph nodes are stable, and your spleen is slightly larger but unchanged from before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So nothing’s blocking or inflamed?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No, the scan looks clear. That’s reassuring. Your shoulder X-ray is also normal—no fracture or arthritis.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So why does it hurt? Could it be lymphoma?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s possible, but unlikely. We’ll keep an eye on it. You may need an MRI later if it doesn’t improve.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that’s a relief. How’s my blood work?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your white count is low—2.2—because of your immune condition. Hemoglobin is a bit low too, but stable. Platelets are okay.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Should I be worried about that?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not acutely. Your levels are consistent with your history. We’ll keep monitoring.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re scheduling your colonoscopy for today. It’s mostly to rule out infection or inflammation since your symptoms haven’t fully resolved.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will they take biopsies?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, they’ll take a few samples. It might help us find a cause if it’s not just a virus.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my IVIG? Is that still happening?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, right after the colonoscopy. You’re getting your full dose.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The colonoscopy was unremarkable. The inside of your bowel looks healthy. No ulcers, masses, or active inflammation.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No sign of lymphoma?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No visible signs. Biopsies are pending, but so far, nothing concerning. We also tested for C. diff and parasites—both negative.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the CMV test?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: CMV came back negative. So it’s not that either.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So what’s causing this?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Most likely a lingering viral or bacterial gastroenteritis. Your immune deficiency makes it harder to clear infections quickly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the antibiotics will help?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, cipro and flagyl cover a broad range of bacteria. We’ll send you home with a full course.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What about the dizziness?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s improved, right? We think it was due to dehydration from diarrhea. Your blood pressure is still low but stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, I feel less lightheaded now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good. We’ll keep an eye on it. Your ostomy site looks better too—less red than when you came in.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Morning. We’re planning to discharge you today. You’re feeling better, stools are firmer, and no new issues.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. What meds am I going home with?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: All your usual meds, plus cipro and flagyl for a week. Also, loperamide for diarrhea and dicyclomine for cramps if needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the Dilaudid? I know it’s limited.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, 18 tablets. Please discuss with your pain doctor about long-term use.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will do. Any follow-up tests?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. We ordered a strongyloides IgG test—important for someone on IVIG. And please follow up on the colonoscopy biopsies.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my shoulder?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: If it doesn’t get better, your doctor may order an MRI. But for now, it’s likely musculoskeletal.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. When should I call the doctor?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: If you develop fever, worsening pain, more diarrhea, or blood in stool—call right away.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my diabetes? Should I restart metformin?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, you can restart it tomorrow. Just monitor your sugars closely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Dr. Lee. I feel much better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. We’ll get your discharge papers ready. You should be out by noon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just a final check before you leave. Any new symptoms?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, all good. Stomach feels better, and I’m not dizzy anymore.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Great. Remember to follow up with your primary doctor in a week.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thanks again for everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care. Feel better soon.
